title: Integrate jieba-rs for Chinese word segmentation

Implement native Chinese G2P (ZHG2P) in Rust
description:
Port misaki's ZHG2P (Chinese Grapheme-to-Phoneme) to pure Rust for native Chinese TTS support.

## Components to Port
1. Word segmentation (jieba-rs available)
2. Pinyin conversion (pinyin crate available)  
3. Number conversion (chinese-number crate available)
4. Tone sandhi rules (~400 lines to port)
5. Pinyin-to-IPA transcription (~250 lines)
6. ZH frontend with erhua handling (~200 lines)

## Estimated Effort
~930 lines of Rust, 5-8 days

## Reference
See history/chinese-g2p-feasibility.md for detailed analysis.

## Model Support
This enables support for Kokoro v1.1-zh Chinese model (103 voices).

## Tasks
1. Add model download to scripts/download_models.sh
2. Add voice download to scripts/download_voices.sh
3. Integrate with koko CLI for zh language selection
4. Test with sample Chinese text

title: Add markdown/markup stripping before TTS synthesis
description: Strip markdown formatting (headers, bold, italic, code blocks, links, etc.) from text before sending to Kokoro for synthesis. Raw markdown symbols like **, ##, ```, etc. should not be spoken aloud.

title: Implement pinyin-to-IPA transcription in Rust
Add AUR publishing to release workflow
Kokoro finetune → distill → runtime (native + oqto wasm)
description:
Goal: fine-tune Kokoro (English + German), distill to a ~7M student, and ship it in kokorox (native Rust via ONNX) and eventually the browser (oqto wasm via ort-wasm) — folding into the spqx voicepack/worker layer where applicable.

Rationale: beating the KittenTTS-from-scratch idea with a more pragmatic train→distill path (proven by oddadmix/Kokoro-7M-Distill). One ONNX artifact serves kokorox (ort crate) + browser (ort-wasm + webworker).

Key constraints / decisions to preserve:
- Keep phoneme vocabulary FROZEN to Kokoro's set so the distilled model and the G2P stay in lockstep (misaki/misaki-rs emit it).
- Runtime must be Rust (kokorox) and compile to wasm (oqto). No Python at inference; training/distillation stays in Python.
- Replace espeak-ng (GPL) with misaki-rs (Apache, Rust, wasm-capable, espeak feature off) — also removes the current GPL-3.0 on the whole binary from espeak-rs-sys.
- spqx is Qwen3/MLX (Apple Silicon); fold at the voicepack + worker-protocol layer, not a model swap.

Children: German finetune, distill test in kokorox, misaki-rs migration, ONNX export + wasm path.

title: Test distilled Kokoro-7M versions in kokorox
description:
Evaluate the oddadmix/Kokoro-7M-Distill (7.48M params, 28.7MB fp32, 24kHz, Apache-2.0) as a runtime model in kokorox.

Steps:
1. Get the distilled model into an ONNX form kokorox can load (the `ort` crate path currently used for 82M). Confirm export/ops (ISTFTNet decoder + LSTM) load in current ONNX Runtime.
2. Verify phoneme-set compatibility with the G2P (misaki-rs) — must match Kokoro's vocab or re-map.
3. Benchmark native: RTF, load time, memory vs current 82M path. Vendor claims ~45x realtime CPU, ~4x faster than 82M — verify on byteowlz hw.
4. Blind/AB quality vs 82M baseline (same lines, unknown A/B) + CER (ASR intelligibility). Only claim quality if a blind test passes: distillation trades quality vs teacher.
5. If good, wire as a selectable runtime model (e.g. --model 7m) and prep for wasm.

Reference: oddadmix/Kokoro-7M-Distill. Distill target ideally from the fine-tuned 82M (English + German children) so voices + language coverage carry over.

title: Fine-tune a German Kokoro model
description:
Fine-tune Kokoro-82M for German.

Base: semidark/kikiri-tts (ex kokoro-deutsch) — a documented StyleTTS2 training fork purpose-built for German (Stage 1 + Stage 2, voicepack extraction). StyleTTS2 MIT, base Kokoro Apache-2.0. See also Jeevav62/tts-finetune-recipes as an English reference pipeline.

Approach:
1. H3 (4090 ComfyUI) generates German reference audio for known transcripts x emotions (transcript known by construction); ASR round-trip filter (>=0.95); loudnorm 24kHz mono shards. Open Yap 1K natural lane if German data is sparse (DUA-bound, no speaker-identifiable cloning).
2. Train a German voice in kikiri-tts on the 4090 (~75 min S1 + ~3h S2 for ~1k clips).
3. Extract voicepack + converted checkpoint.

Deliverables:
- Trained German Kokoro checkpoint + voicepack.
- German G2P path — German phonemization currently goes through espeak-ng (see misaki-rs migration child); verify phoneme-set compatibility.
- Verify quality/latency in kokorox.

Deps: dataset lane (H3 samples); non-GPL runtime via misaki-rs migration.

title: Migrate G2P to misaki-rs, drop espeak-ng (GPL) dependency
description:
Replace the espeak-ng G2P with misaki-rs (Apache-2.0 Rust port of misaki, self-contained, POS-aware, en-us/en-gb, wasm-capable) with the espeak feature compiled OUT.

Why:
- The whole kokorox binary is currently GPL-3.0 ONLY because of espeak-rs-sys (statically links espeak-ng, GPL-3.0). Removing it returns kokorox to a permissive license and unlocks wasm distribution.
- misaki-rs compiles to wasm (pure Rust, no system dep), which is required for the oqto browser path.
- Emits Kokoro's frozen phoneme vocabulary — keeps G2P and any distilled model in lockstep.

Scope:
1. Swap espeak-rs-sys / espeak-ng path for misaki-rs (default-features=false).
2. Keep multi-language story: English via misaki-rs; check/plan per-language G2P (ZH/JA/etc may still need native ports — see existing kokorox-bz9 Chinese G2P; German must be covered for the German finetune).
3. Verify OOV fallback behavior (letter-spelling) acceptable or add small neural OOV later.
4. Update README/license claims (currently states GPL-3.0).
5. Ship as part of the wasm build target.

title: Export finetuned/distilled Kokoro to ONNX and add wasm (ort-wasm) browser path
description:
Ship the trained (English + German) and distilled Kokoro as a single ONNX artifact that runs both native in kokorox and in the browser (oqto) via wasm.

Steps:
1. Export the fine-tuned 82M and the distilled student from PyTorch to ONNX (matching the ops kokorox's `ort` crate already loads).
2. Quantize for a slim wasm artifact (int8/fp16) — 7M-distill is ~29MB fp32 / ~8MB int8.
3. Verify ISTFTNet decoder + LSTM ops run under ort-wasm (ONNX Runtime Web) — may need to pin an ORT version; reference the proven onnx-kokoro-web / kokoro-js / kokoro-onnx browser paths.
4. Wire into kokorox as a selectable runtime model (e.g. --model 7m / --model 82m).
5. Add a wasm32 build target (wasm-bindgen) + a webworker TTS entrypoint for oqto.
6. Constraints: phoneme vocab stays frozen to Kokoro's set; G2P via misaki-rs (Apache, wasm) — no espeak at inference.

Depends on: misaki-rs migration (kokorox-wz8y.3) for a clean non-GPL wasm build; distilled-model test (kokorox-wz8y.1) to pick the artifact.

title: Add a spqx-compatible binary-framed TTS worker binary
description:
Per foxline docs/adr/0012-tts-engine-contract-unification.md, kokorox must expose the same persistent worker protocol as spqx-tts-worker so hosts (foxline) can launch either engine interchangeably as a drop-in process.

Protocol (match spqx exactly):
- Frame header: u8 type, u32 request_id, u32 payload_len, little-endian (9 bytes), then payload.
- Input frames: speak(1) with JSON payload (text, optional voice/language/speed), cancel(2), shutdown(3).
- Output frames: ready(1, carries negotiated sample rate), audio_start(2), audio_chunk(3, PCM16 LE mono), audio_done(4), error(5). JSON status events on stderr only; stdout carries frames exclusively.

Scope:
- New binary (e.g. kokorox-tts-worker) built on TTSManager; one model loaded at a time, honoring speak/cancel/shutdown like the spqx worker, including cancellation mid-stream.
- --model / --voices / --lan flags mirroring the koko CLI; German finetunes (e.g. crane-local-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-German-ONNX with voices/df_kerstin.bin) must load through the same flags.

Proof of positive outcome:
- A test harness (or foxline's worker client) drives speak -> streamed chunks -> audio_done, then cancel mid-generation and asserts no further audio_chunk frames for the canceled request id.
- Golden-wave test: same text/voice/speed through worker and koko CLI produce identical PCM.
- A German finetune (kokoro-martin.onnx or crane model.onnx + df_kerstin.bin) synthesizes intelligible German through the worker; sample file committed to test fixtures or recorded in the issue.

title: Exit GPL: replace the espeak-rs static link and relicense to Apache-2.0
description:
kokorox is GPL-3.0 solely because espeak-rs 0.1.9 statically links espeak-ng; everything else (ort/MIT, Kokoro weights and German finetunes/Apache) is permissive. foxline ADR 0012 keeps kokorox a separate process for exactly this reason; removing the static link lets kokorox relicense to Apache-2.0 and removes the process-boundary caveat for distributors.

Options (in preference order):
1. Shell out to an installed espeak-ng binary via a persistent subprocess (phonemization is ms-fast; GPL stays a separate program, mere aggregation). Keeps espeak-grade phonemes that the German finetunes were trained on.
2. For German specifically, port/borrow Crane's MIT hand-built German G2P (lucasjinreal/Crane, pure Rust; crane-local-ai German model card notes only minor IPA drift vs espeak: stress placement, diacritics, r-realization).
3. misaki (hexgrad, Apache-2.0) for en/ja/zh/ko long-term; no German support upstream, Python-only today.

Scope:
- Make the phonemizer pluggable behind a trait; ship the chosen non-GPL default; keep espeak paths opt-in without a static link.
- Update Cargo license fields, README license section, and crate metadata after the last GPL dependency is gone.

Proof of positive outcome:
- cargo tree / cargo deny (or equivalent license audit) shows no GPL-linked crates in the default feature set.
- cargo build succeeds on Linux and macOS without espeak-ng dev libraries installed (subprocess option) or with no system espeak at all (G2P option).
- German regression: synthesize a fixed German corpus (dates, units, Euro amounts, abbreviations like Prof./Min./ltr.) with the old espeak build and the new default; ASR round-trip or side-by-side listening confirms no intelligibility loss; results recorded in this issue.
- License fields and README updated to Apache-2.0 (with attribution note for espeak-ng where the subprocess path is used).

title: Add a spqx-compatible binary-framed TTS worker binary
description:
Implement the existing spqx/PiBot binary worker contract (Foxline ADR 0012), without inventing a JSON speak dialect.

Verified source contract:
- Header: u8 type, u32 request_id, u32 payload_len, little-endian (9 bytes).
- speak(1): raw UTF-8 text. cancel(2)/shutdown(3): empty payload.
- ready(1): empty payload, id zero. audio_start(2): u32 LE sample rate. audio_chunk(3): PCM16 LE mono. audio_done(4): empty terminal completion, including canceled requests. error(5): UTF-8 terminal failure.
- Voice/language/speed are launch flags, not per-request JSON fields. stdout frames only; diagnostics on stderr.

Implementation: kokorox-worker workspace crate with kokorox-tts-worker executable; explicit local model/NPZ voice assets; v1.0 vocabulary and 24000 Hz initially. TTSKoko::tts_stream_audio emits completed inference chunks; ONNX kernels are not preemptible but obsolete output is fenced. Fixed-size request queue and frame bounds; unknown cancellation IDs do not accumulate.

Proof required before closure:
1. Protocol fixtures for UTF-8, rate payload, PCM clipping, bounded parsing, errors, active/queued cancel, next-request reuse, shutdown fencing and clean EOF drain.
2. Real binary test demonstrating stdout isolation and structured startup failure.
3. Deterministic base-model test comparing buffered, callback-streamed and worker PCM.
4. German model smoke + independent ASR/listening, not invented quality claims. Martin ships a directly usable NPZ (510,1,256); its graph has random operators so independent PCM parity is not meaningful. Crane's raw float32 df_kerstin.bin needs conversion to NPZ and is not validated here.
5. cargo check --workspace, core tests, worker tests, focused clippy, release build; document missing platform/GPU proof. Generated models/audio stay outside git.

Foxline adapter and Persona integration remain fxl-8bht/fxl-00hv; this issue alone does not establish a complete Foxline conversation or cross-platform Qwen performance.

title: Audit licensing/provenance and replace the espeak-rs static link
description:
Foxline ADR 0012 keeps kokorox separate from spqx. The README says GPL due to espeak-rs-sys statically linking espeak-ng, while existing Cargo manifests say Apache-2.0. Reconcile that mismatch with an actual transitive-license and source-provenance audit; no automatic relicensing claim.

Scope:
- Audit dependencies, retained source notices and contributor rights. Removing espeak does not grant permission to relicense any existing GPL-covered source.
- Evaluate an external espeak-ng invocation versus a permissive German G2P (Crane declares MIT). Verify exact code/assets licenses before reuse; evaluate model-trained IPA conventions and quality.
- Misaki declares Apache-2.0 but optional fallbacks can use espeak; audit backends rather than treating a top-level license as sufficient.
- Preserve GPL obligations for shipped espeak binaries/data. Separate processes are an implementation boundary, not blanket proof of mere aggregation or lawful distribution.
- Update README/Cargo metadata/LICENSE/attributions only to the extent established by the audit and rightsholder authorization.

Proof:
- Record a dependency-license report plus retained source/provenance findings and any authorization needed.
- Non-linked alternative builds on macOS/Linux without espeak development libraries; external executable prerequisites documented.
- Test G2P and German audio on fixed corpus including abbreviations, numbers, dates, units and currencies; quantify ASR/listening regressions.
- Treat browser/WASM packaging as its own compliance review. GPL is not an automatic ban on browser use, nor is removing espeak automatically sufficient for an Apache bundle.

title: Align package license metadata with the current GPL declaration
description: Current root LICENSE/README declare GPLv3 and native worker uses GPL-3.0-only, while four other Cargo manifests and WebSocket README claim Apache-2.0. Centralize the current workspace declaration, inherit it across all five packages, and correct docs without claiming MIT clearance or revoking historical permissive grants. Proof: cargo metadata --no-deps resolves all five licenses to GPL-3.0-only; just license-metadata-check passes; executable negative fixtures reject a stale member and a root/member mismatch; just check and just worker-test pass. Broader espeak-free MIT source/dependency/data audit stays kokorox-8j45.

title: Prototype espeak-free English/German G2P with model-compatible IPA
description: User wants to remove espeak entirely and target an MIT-licensed engine for Oqto/browser integration; umbrella kokorox-8j45. Start with an isolated prototype rather than claiming the existing engine is already relicensable. Audit/extract only needed MIT Crane frontend code at pinned revision 2ee897a08e7b1df1c7cd2beca2aedd5dfe2e774d, preserving notices. No dependency on the full inference framework and no espeak code/dictionary copy or silent subprocess fallback. Crane German lexicon is CC BY-SA 4.0, not MIT: begin with rule-only evaluation or an independently verified permissive asset; separately licensed data needs an explicit packaging/provenance decision. English dictionary permissions must be verified against the exact asset provenance, not generalized from top-level metadata. Keep shared normalization and model-specific stress/affricate/diphthong adaptation distinct. Inventory existing languages and retain independently supported Chinese/Japanese paths; do not silently drop other languages or fall back to English. Proof: fixed held-out English/German corpus covering names, compounds, abbreviations, numbers, dates, units, currencies and punctuation; negative unsupported-language tests; real Martin synthesis compared against current frontend with ASR error counts, TTFA/RTF and listening review. Martin is stochastic, so do not require independent PCM equality. Demonstrate dependency/build/artifact absence of espeak on macOS/Linux without dev libraries and unchanged worker raw-text/ready/rate/cancel protocol. WASM implementation and lawful final relicensing are separate gates. See docs/licensing-transition.md.

title: Keep static LAME out of the permissive inference and browser profile
description: Preliminary audit for kokorox-8j45 found unconditional mp3lame-encoder 0.2.1 / mp3lame-sys 0.1.9 in core; the sys build emits static=mp3lame and declares LGPL-3.0. Even PCM-only kokorox-worker reaches it. LGPL is not GPL and does not forbid MIT application code, but leaves source/relinking/distribution obligations inconsistent with claiming a permissive-only browser artifact. Remove/replace MP3 encoding from the minimal core or isolate it behind an explicit non-default optional encoding profile with correct notices. Do not silently change OpenAI API default MP3 behavior, pretend WAV is MP3, or discard format options; preserve supported behavior or document a deliberate migration and reject disabled formats clearly. Proof: cargo tree plus build/link/artifact evidence show no LAME in minimal worker/browser dependency graph; PCM/WAV inference and worker tests pass; API tests cover enabled MP3 and disabled unsupported-format errors; benchmark hot inference unaffected; inspect actual target assets/JS glue before declaring WASM clearance. No source-relicensing claim solely from this dependency change.

title: Establish retained-source rights and notices for the MIT transition
description: User authorizes an MIT target, but current history alone does not establish permission for every retained source file. Parent audit kokorox-8j45; docs/licensing-transition.md. Record source origins and exact grants: initial Cargo lacked a license field, root Apache-2.0 introduced at 2586d28, GPL root replaced it at 72b36e0, Cargo metadata remained Apache. Current upstream license API is absent; that does not revoke established historical grants, but requires verifying historical source permissions rather than assuming a blanket grant. Examine pre-GPL upstream contributions and post-GPL adaptations; Git author identities are not ownership proof. In particular audit Chinese tone_sandhi.rs attribution to Misaki/PaddleSpeech and preserve their required licenses/notices. Separate maintainer-authorized changes from GPL-only code needing permission or independent replacement. Store contributor contacts/ownership correspondence privately; publish only safe commit/path/grant evidence and required public attribution. Proof: per-file/component provenance inventory, retained third-party license/NOTICE texts, documented authorizations or replacements, exact release source/artifact mapping and review of code/data/model/transitive/native licenses. Only after rights plus frontend/encoding/quality gates pass may root/package metadata change to the authorized permissive terms. Earlier releases keep their actual licenses/source. Do not claim metadata correction or replacing espeak automatically grants MIT permission.

title: Remove espeak and establish a lawful MIT-targeted release
description:
Foxline ADR 0012 keeps kokorox separate from spqx. The README says GPL due to espeak-rs-sys statically linking espeak-ng, while existing Cargo manifests say Apache-2.0. Reconcile that mismatch with an actual transitive-license and source-provenance audit; no automatic relicensing claim.

Scope:
- Audit dependencies, retained source notices and contributor rights. Removing espeak does not grant permission to relicense any existing GPL-covered source.
- Evaluate an external espeak-ng invocation versus a permissive German G2P (Crane declares MIT). Verify exact code/assets licenses before reuse; evaluate model-trained IPA conventions and quality.
- Misaki declares Apache-2.0 but optional fallbacks can use espeak; audit backends rather than treating a top-level license as sufficient.
- Preserve GPL obligations for shipped espeak binaries/data. Separate processes are an implementation boundary, not blanket proof of mere aggregation or lawful distribution.
- Update README/Cargo metadata/LICENSE/attributions only to the extent established by the audit and rightsholder authorization.

Proof:
- Record a dependency-license report plus retained source/provenance findings and any authorization needed.
- Non-linked alternative builds on macOS/Linux without espeak development libraries; external executable prerequisites documented.
- Test G2P and German audio on fixed corpus including abbreviations, numbers, dates, units and currencies; quantify ASR/listening regressions.
- Treat browser/WASM packaging as its own compliance review. GPL is not an automatic ban on browser use, nor is removing espeak automatically sufficient for an Apache bundle.

User decision: target MIT for code the project can lawfully license that way and remove espeak rather than relying on an external espeak process. Preliminary findings are recorded in docs/licensing-transition.md. Current metadata is corrected under kokorox-m9bx; do not confuse that with relicensing. Implementation gates: kokorox-1tgn (audited espeak-free English/German G2P and real-model quality), kokorox-21eq (LAME-free minimal/core/browser profile), kokorox-11rz (source rights/notices). Crane code is MIT, but German dictionary data is CC BY-SA 4.0; data permissions must not be silently generalized from code licenses. Current native worker still links espeak; no MIT/WASM-ready engine claim yet.

title: Align package license metadata with the current GPL declaration
description: Current root LICENSE/README declare GPLv3 and native worker uses GPL-3.0-only, while four other Cargo manifests and WebSocket README claim Apache-2.0. Centralize the current workspace declaration, inherit it across all five packages, and correct docs without claiming MIT clearance or revoking historical permissive grants. Proof: cargo metadata --no-deps resolves all five licenses to GPL-3.0-only; just license-metadata-check passes; executable negative fixtures reject a stale member and a root/member mismatch; just check and just worker-test pass. Broader espeak-free MIT source/dependency/data audit stays kokorox-8j45.
close_reason: Current root/workspace metadata and docs reconciled at 64a540d; positive/negative regression probes, workspace check and worker tests pass. MIT transition remains kokorox-8j45 and its implementation gates.
